tasks.title: Recover surviving work from disk and Git before finalizing the task register.
tasks.scope_and_completion:
Inspect both known local repositories, their worktrees, uncommitted files, branches, stashes, reflogs and unreachable objects without cleanup or resets. Inspect current and older scratch directories, source-review folders, raw numerical results, test logs, manifests, viewer exports and packaged versions. Enumerate all remote branches and all PRs, including closed-unmerged attempts; distinguish work already incorporated by later commits from genuinely missing changes. Check issues and unfinished workflow runs. Use targeted interruption/session logs only to resolve artifacts whose purpose or final command outcome is unclear. Check additional project-linked checkouts discovered through worktree metadata; do not assume the two familiar folders are the entire history. Follow docs/DOCUMENTATION_STATUS.md: executable implementation/tests take precedence over stale inventories. **Recovery gate:** every discovered project location and work family has a disposition; each branch with unique changes is either preserved for review, proven superseded, or explicitly unresolved. Do not turn a keyword hit or an unreachable Git object into a new task without examining it.
   Start with the existing G1–G8, W1–W3, A1–A2, P1, T1–T3, S1–S2, H1–H2, C1–C2, F1–F2, R1–R2 and V1 ledger. Link each record to its latest code, report, inputs, tests and publication status. Classify the 607 inventoried files by experiment family, deduplicate copies, and distinguish commitments from suggested follow-ons. Check older repository questions against current code before reopening them. Give every open task a next action, dependency, completion criterion and blocker. **Done when:** each recovered commitment has one current disposition and superseded status has an explicit replacement. This plan is the starting queue; detailed file-by-file reconciliation remains work.

tasks.latest_result: Finite-source mixed-size network now has a duration audit and an analytical depletion bound: at gain 4, feedback becomes no stronger than damping by s*log(6)/.15 seconds, at most 11.945 seconds for the current four nodes. This is conditional on the existing model scope and rules out indefinite powering without replenishment; physical breathing and calibrated supply remain open. See docs/fold_duration.md and docs/experiments/fold-duration-summary.json for numerical results. All active/passive/rest runs completed 60 seconds; active reserves crossed 1 percent at about 15.2-28.0 seconds and mechanical energy decreased after the bound. Root error 5.331e-14 J, finer 5.072e-15 J; 18 tests passed. Sustained breathing remains unproven.
